title: Larchwood Roasters
goal: Ten strangers order our coffee online — and come back for a second bag.
decisions: A static site with Stripe Checkout, no backend of our own: orders arrive as Stripe payments and emails.
Stripe test mode until the company is verified; live keys only after the bank confirms.

nodes.title: A stranger orders a bag from the site
nodes.done_when: someone we do not know pays for a bag without our help
nodes.note: The first milestone: the shortest path from opening the site to a paid order.

children.title: Landing page: our story and three coffees
children.note: Headline «Small-batch coffee, roasted every Tuesday», our story in three sentences, Ethiopia Guji, Colombia Huila and House Espresso with prices. The site lives in site/.

children.title: Product cards and cart
children.done_when: add two bags, the total is right
children.note: Each coffee gets a card with roast, notes and price, and an «Add to cart» button; the cart keeps bags and shows the total.

children.title: Checkout with Stripe (test mode)
children.done_when: a test card payment shows up as an order
children.note: Stripe Checkout from the cart; the success page thanks the customer and says when the bag ships.

children.title: Domain and hosting
children.done_when: the site opens on our domain over https

children.title: Show the site to three friends, watch silently
children.done_when: three people ordered without asking us a question — or we know what stopped them

nodes.title: Second orders: subscription and emails
nodes.done_when: a customer orders a second bag without being reminded by us

children.title: Subscription: a bag every two weeks
children.done_when: a test subscriber is charged again two weeks later

children.title: Order emails
children.done_when: an order sends a confirmation and a «roasted and shipped» email
